questions.stem: Sodium has an atomic number of 11. What is its electronic structure?
questions.explanation: Sodium has 11 electrons. The first shell holds a maximum of 2 electrons, the second shell holds a maximum of 8 electrons, and the remaining 1 electron goes into the third shell. This gives the electronic structure 2, 8, 1. Shells are always filled from the innermost shell outwards.

questions.stem: An element has the electronic structure 2, 8, 7. Which group of the Periodic Table does it belong to?
questions.explanation: The group number equals the number of electrons in the outermost shell. This element has 7 electrons in its outer shell, so it is in Group 7 (the halogens). With a total of 17 electrons, this is chlorine. Note: Group 7 is sometimes called Group 17 in modern numbering, but at GCSE level, Group 7 is the standard answer.

questions.stem: Why do elements in the same group of the Periodic Table have similar chemical properties?

options.text: They have the same number of electron shells
They have the same total number of electrons
They have the same number of electrons in their outer shell
They have the same number of neutrons

questions.explanation: Elements in the same group have the same number of electrons in their outermost shell. Since chemical reactions involve outer shell electrons (through transfer or sharing), elements with the same number of outer electrons react in similar ways. The number of shells determines the period, not the group.

questions.stem: An atom has the electronic structure 2, 8, 8. What can you deduce about this element?

options.text: It is a very reactive metal in Group 8
It is a noble gas with a full outer shell, making it very unreactive
It is a halogen that readily gains one electron
It is in Period 2 of the Periodic Table

questions.explanation: The electronic structure 2, 8, 8 has a full outer shell (8 electrons in the third shell). This is argon, a noble gas in Group 0. Noble gases are very unreactive because their outer electron shell is complete, so they have no tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons. It is in Period 3 (three shells), not Period 2.

questions.stem: Element X has the electronic structure 2, 4. Element Y has the electronic structure 2, 8, 4. Which statement is correct?

options.text: X and Y are in different groups and different periods
X and Y are in the same group but different periods
X and Y are in the same period but different groups
X and Y are the same element

questions.explanation: Both elements have 4 electrons in their outer shell, placing them in the same group (Group 4). Element X has 2 shells (Period 2 - this is carbon), while Element Y has 3 shells (Period 3 - this is silicon). Elements in the same group but different periods have similar chemical properties because they share the same number of outer shell electrons.
